cypher.trail.state: Documented dialect difference; other deviations need review
cypher.trail.note: The expectation uses relationship uniqueness within one MATCH. Ladybug documents walk semantics by default. An extra match under that dialect is not automatically a defect. Crabgraph deviations still need an explicit semantic decision.

cypher.labels.note: Ladybug documents label(node), whereas this probe uses Neo4j's labels(node). Query rejection here does not mean Ladybug has no label inspection.

gremlin.empty_sum.state: Reproduced against reference; root cause open
gremlin.empty_sum.note: TinkerGraph 3.7.4 emits no result for this empty sum. SQLg 3.1.6 returned a NaN value, serialized as a string by the adapter. This is a reference-observed difference; investigate SQL aggregation and serialization before assigning a defect.

gremlin.local.note: The expected local sums are 3 and 3, corroborated by TinkerGraph 3.7.4. SQLg 3.1.6 returns one row containing 6. Disabling only SqlgLocalStepStrategy restores two rows containing 3 on the same graph and adapter. This isolates the observed divergence to that optimization path.

gremlin.missing_order.note: SQLg documents an error when order().by() refers to a nonexistent property, whereas TinkerGraph filters unproductive traversers. Treat this as a provider behavior difference.
